title: The Debt of the Green Zone Anew
premise: Gideon Quintana, a whistle-blower living under four names, receives a meeting invitation from her dead handler, Mara Voss, and walks into a trap set by the very agency she once exposed. The invitation is bait: someone inside the network is planning to destroy the Green Zone water treatment facility during the upcoming summit and stage it as an infrastructure accident. Hunted by both the conspirators and the investigators chasing Voss's murder, Gideon must decide whether to trust Elias Brandt, the investigator who once tried to burn her, or go it alone. In the end she exposes the plot at the summit itself, sacrifices her fourth identity to save the facility, and chooses testimony over disappearance — trading her anonymity for justice.
about_author: Petra Kavanagh is a former humanitarian logistics coordinator who spent six years in conflict zones before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about ordinary people trapped inside systems designed to forget them.

chapters.title: Four Names, One Bag
chapters.summary: POV: Gideon. We meet Gideon in her carefully constructed life as 'Nadia Reyes,' a translator in a coastal city: packed go-bag, burner phone, rehearsed cover story. A routine check of her dead-drop reveals an encrypted meeting request signed by Mara Voss — who died eleven days ago. The emotional beat is dread sharpened by grief; the chapter ends with Gideon deciding, against every instinct, that she has to know who sent it.

chapters.title: The Invitation from a Corpse
chapters.summary: POV: Gideon. She verifies the message's cryptographic signature — genuinely Voss's key, post-dated after her death. Following the coordinates to an abandoned ferry terminal, she finds not Voss but a staged scene: surveillance photos of herself under all four names, and a summit security briefing marked with the treatment plant's schematics. Beat: vertigo — someone owns her completely. She pockets the schematics and runs as headlights sweep the pier.

chapters.title: Elias Brandt Doesn't Knock
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Gideon and Elias. Investigator Elias Brandt, reopening the Voss case, traces the same signal and corners Gideon at a safehouse. Their history is hostile — he built the case that forced her into hiding. He offers uneasy alliance: Voss was murdered because she found something about the summit. Beat: grudging, electric distrust; they agree to a 48-hour truce sealed by mutual leverage.

chapters.title: What Voss Buried
chapters.summary: POV: Elias. Elias decrypts Voss's personal archive: evidence that a private security consortium contracted for summit protection plans a catastrophic 'accident' at the Green Zone water plant to trigger emergency privatization contracts. Among the files, a name Gideon recognizes — her own third identity, listed as a patsy. Beat: cold fury; the frame was years in the making, and Voss died trying to warn her.

chapters.title: The Man with Her Old Face
chapters.summary: POV: Gideon. To access the consortium's front company, Gideon resurrects identity number three — 'Claire Ostend' — knowing it paints a target on her. Inside their offices she finds the accident timeline moved up: 36 hours, before the summit's opening session. She's nearly caught by a handler who knew Claire personally. Beat: terror braided with exhilaration; living a lie again feels horrifyingly easy.

chapters.title: Loyalty Has a Price List
chapters.summary: POV: Elias. Elias discovers his own supervisor is on the consortium's payroll and that his investigation was sanctioned as controlled opposition. Confronted privately, the supervisor offers him promotion and Gideon's head. Beat: betrayal and temptation; Elias records the conversation instead of accepting, but realizes he can no longer trust any official channel — the law itself is compromised.

chapters.title: Thirty-Six Hours
chapters.summary: POV: Gideon. Racing the clock, Gideon and Elias map the plant's maintenance tunnels and identify the sabotage method: pressure sensors rigged to fail catastrophically during a routine flush. But the plan requires someone with legitimate access codes — and the insider is a plant engineer Gideon once protected during her whistle-blowing days. Beat: moral weight; saving the plant may mean exposing another person like her old self.

chapters.title: The Turncoat's Dilemma
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. They confront the engineer, Tomas, who confesses he was coerced via threats to his family. Instead of turning him in, Gideon proposes using his access to feed false confirmation to the conspirators while Elias physically disables the rig. The counter-operation goes live — until the consortium detects the anomaly and moves the detonation window forward by hours. Beat: hope curdling into panic.

chapters.title: Green Water Rising
chapters.summary: POV: Gideon. Climax. With the summit convening overhead, Gideon enters the plant alone when the remote fails, wading through rising floodwater to manually vent the pressure as the consortium's strike team hunts her through the tunnels. Elias holds off security forces by broadcasting Voss's decrypted files to every press feed at the summit. Beat: visceral, breathless sacrifice; Gideon triggers the failsafe as the ceiling section gives way above her.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: POV: Gideon. Resolution. Gideon survives, injured, as the leaked files ignite arrests across three countries. Offered extraction into yet another new life, she declines — walking into a public hearing under her real name, first time spoken aloud in seven years, to testify against the consortium. Tomas reunites with his family; Elias closes the Voss case with the truth. Final beat: quiet liberation — the go-bag stays unpacked by the door, just in case, but she finally sleeps without one ear open.
